content: When a shared helper swallows failure on purpose, callers that must know the outcome cannot learn it from the return value. Publish the outcome separately - a status variable, an out-param, a structured result - and have those callers test that. Do NOT fix it by making the helper return non-zero: under set -e that aborts every caller invoking it bare, which is the failure the tolerance existed to prevent. When you read a guard of the form 'if ! tolerant_helper', check the helper's return contract before trusting the branch.
context: dply_apt_update in BuildsProvisionScriptPreamble deliberately returns 0 on every path so a flaky third-party repo cannot abort a step running bare under set -e. pinMysqlSeries then guarded its cleanup with 'if ! dply_apt_update; then rm -f dply-mysql.list'. That branch could never execute, so an expired MySQL signing key left a permanently unverifiable repo in sources.list.d and broke every later apt-get update on the host. It read as working code and had shipped that way.
title: A helper that always returns 0 needs a status sentinel, or its callers' error branches are dead code
